customManagers.description: The structurizr.war the `structurizr` CI job runs, pinned by STRUCTURIZR_VERSION under a `# renovate:` comment. Structurizr tags its application releases `vYYYY.MM.DD` and its library releases `vX.Y.Z` in the same repository; the regex versioning keeps only the dated ones. A new WAR can change what `pnpm fixtures:acceptance` writes, and then the job fails until the pull request commits the regenerated fixture.

packageRules.description: Keep the pinned action digests current. Every third-party action in .github/workflows is pinned to a full commit SHA for OpenSSF Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check; without this rule those pins rot into a security liability instead of being one. One PR, monthly, since they move together and none of them ship into user output.

packageRules.description: Development tooling: lint, types, commit plumbing. None of it reaches a rendered workspace, so one grouped PR per week is enough review surface.

The rendering runtime. These are the packages whose code is inlined into the page a user publishes, so each one gets its own PR, which keeps a bad update easy to find and revert — never grouped, never rolled up with anything else.

@dagrejs/* is pinned to exact versions in package.json on purpose: `src/engine/layout/automatic.ts` imports Dagre's internal `lib/order` modules, which carry no semver promise. Renovate replaces the exact version with a new exact version; it must never widen the pin into a range.
`engines` states the supported Node and pnpm range — a compatibility promise made in README.md and enforced by the CI matrix. Raising it is a decision, not a dependency update.

Auto-merge every patch, minor, pin and digest update, for npm and GitHub Actions alike, runtime packages included. CI is the review: nothing merges without the `ci` check, which runs the whole suite and both render modes, and `minimumReleaseAge` keeps anything from merging the day it is published (14 days for @dagrejs/*). Majors and lock file maintenance stay manual: a major changes APIs and behavior, and those pull requests still need a person.
